last_amended.value: 88th Legislature, Regular Session (2023). Confirm against current chapter for any amendments enacted since.
last_amended.notes: Texas Legislature meets biennially. Most recent regular session was 2023. Verify current text before relying.

acknowledgment_deadline.notes: Statute requires production 'promptly' under § 552.221(a). If records cannot be produced within 10 business days, the governmental body must certify that in writing and state a date when records will be available — that 10-business-day check-in is treated by AG opinions as the practical acknowledgment deadline. Mark uncertain because 'promptly' is the literal text and 'reasonably' is judicially construed.

substantive_deadline.notes: Statute requires 'prompt' production with no fixed number of days. 10 business days is the practical norm derived from § 552.221(d) and AG opinions, but it is not a statutory deadline for production itself. Needs legal review before being surfaced to users as 'the deadline.'

extension_rules.value: If the governmental body believes records are excepted from disclosure, it must request an AG ruling within 10 business days of receiving the request. Failure to timely request a ruling presumptively makes records public. § 552.301.

expedited_processing.value: Not provided by statute. Texas PIA does not have a federal-style expedited processing category.
expedited_processing.citation: Tex. Gov't Code Ch. 552 (absence of provision)

constructive_denial.value: If the governmental body fails to request an AG ruling within 10 business days, the records are presumed public absent a compelling reason.

search_fees.value: Charges allowed for personnel time at the rate set by the Office of the Attorney General; first hour of personnel time is free if the request is for 50 or fewer pages of readily available material.
search_fees.citation: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.261; 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 70.3
search_fees.notes: Fee schedule is set by OAG regulation, not the statute. Confirm current Texas Administrative Code rate before quoting.

copy_fees.value: Standard paper copy fees set by OAG rules. The statute caps and structures, OAG regulations fix the per-page amount.
copy_fees.citation: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.262; 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 70.3

fee_waiver.value: Governmental body may waive or reduce charges if it determines waiver is in the public interest because providing the information primarily benefits the general public.

advance_payment_threshold.value: Governmental body may require deposit or bond when estimated cost exceeds $100.
advance_payment_threshold.notes: Threshold figure subject to amendment; verify current statute.

accepted_methods.notes: Request must be in writing. Statute specifies mail, email to designated address, hand delivery, or a designated electronic submission method. § 552.234 governs designation of submission channels.

required_identification.value: Requester need not state purpose. Identification is not required to make a request.

agency_designation.value: Requests must go to the 'public information officer' designated by the governmental body holding the records. The Office of the Attorney General maintains guidance on identifying the officer.

value.name: Confidential by law
value.summary: Information confidential by law (constitutional, statutory, or judicial decision).

value.name: Personnel matters
value.summary: Personnel information whose disclosure would be a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.

value.name: Litigation / settlement
value.summary: Information related to pending or reasonably anticipated litigation.

value.name: Competitive bidding
value.summary: Information that, if released, would give competitive advantage in a bidding context.

value.name: Real estate transactions
value.summary: Information about location of property for acquisition by the governmental body.

value.name: Audit working papers
value.summary: Audit working papers of the State Auditor, county auditors, etc.

value.name: Personal information
value.summary: Home addresses, phone numbers, and family info of public employees and officials who elect protection.

value.name: Law enforcement
value.summary: Records of pending or active law enforcement investigations and prosecutions.

value.name: Other enumerated exceptions
value.summary: Multiple additional category-specific exceptions. Full enumeration required before drafting an appeal.

categories.notes: Texas has ~60 enumerated exceptions. This is a representative subset for v0; full enumeration is required before the product can claim completeness.

burden_of_proof.value: Governmental body bears the burden to establish that requested information is excepted. The AG ruling process places the obligation on the governmental body to articulate and support each claimed exception.

segregability_rule.value: If only a portion of information is excepted, the governmental body must redact the excepted portions and disclose the remainder.

administrative_path.value: Requester may file a complaint with the Office of the Attorney General Open Records Division. The OAG issues binding rulings on whether records must be released.

judicial_path.value: Mandamus action in district court to compel disclosure. The OAG or the requester may file suit if a governmental body refuses to release information after an AG ruling.

attorneys_fees.value: Court may award costs and reasonable attorney fees to a substantially prevailing plaintiff.

requester_eligibility.value: Any person. Public information is available to the public 'at a minimum during the normal business hours of the governmental body.' No residency or citizenship requirement.

open_questions.question: Confirm the canonical 'response deadline' framing for TPIA. The statute's 'promptly' standard plus the 10-business-day check-in rule needs a legally-defensible product-level rule before we tell users a number.
Enumerate all current §§ 552.101-552.158 exceptions; the v0 subset is illustrative only.
